title: Extending RAJA Parallel Programming Abstractions with Just-In-Time Optimization
problem: AOT parallel programming models cannot perform context-specific optimizations due to lack of runtime information
motivation: Heterogeneous computing dominance requires performance portability without sacrificing per-hardware optimizations
method: They integrated Proteus (a runtime compiler based on LLVM) with RAJA, a layer that lets parallel code run across different hardware platforms. At runtime, Proteus applies dimension specialization: it replaces generic variables for loop sizes with the specific numbers determined when code starts executing, enabling highly optimized code tailored to those exact dimensions.
key_novelty: Using a runtime compiler to optimize portable parallel code by specializing loops for the actual dimensions available when code executes.
contributions: Extends RAJA to support JIT-deferred compilation
Demonstrates speedups on both AMD and NVIDIA GPUs
limitations: Evaluation limited to RAJAPerf benchmarks; impact on real applications unclear
